newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firm on bank client demand.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firm on bank client demand.

text.p: The rouble firmed in lively trading on Wednesday as banks sought funds for their clients, dealers said.
"It looks like client demand caused by (month-end) tax payments," ABN-Amro Bank dealer Artur Lotov said.
He added speculative buying had also pushed up overnight credit rates, which yielded 40-55 percent compared with an early 50-65 percent and Tuesday's late 15-25 percent.
Another dealer said the rouble had edged up against the dollar on client buying as well.
"Some bank could be selling dollars for its clients. We do not see any other reasons," he said.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,446-49 per dollar compared with an early 5,452-54 and 5,458-59 late on Tuesday. Tomorrow roubles edged up to 5,455-57 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,456-59.
The central bank said it had set 5,449/5,461 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Wednesday.
